name: Plumber

pf.license.need: Plumbing work in a home needs a license where the state or city licenses plumbers. Gas line work can need its own license or endorsement.
pf.license.who holds it: Both: the company (a plumbing contractor license, where the state asks) and each plumber (apprentice, journeyman or master).
what to ask: The company's license number and class
Each plumber's own number and level, in their invite reply
A gas-line endorsement, where the state has one
pf.license.how it's checked: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, insurance or registration (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
pf.license.blocks going live: The company's plumbing listing goes live once it's set up. Each plumber is offered only once the owner says yes.
pf.license.renewals: Reminders before each expiry, on the dates the owner picks (the example: 5 weeks and 1 week before). A lapsed license pauses new bookings for that person.
pf.license.insurance or bond: Liability insurance, and a bond where the state's form asks for one: from the state form.
pf.license.background checks: Only where the state's form asks.
pf.license.at the counter: Work done at the shop counter: the state's form says if it needs a license. Safe default: the company's license on file, shown on the listing.
pf.license.local rules: Some cities and counties license plumbers or need a permit of their own: the form for that place applies, by the customer's address.

pf.services.capacity: One plumber per booking. Bigger jobs can need a crew of two; the counter's restores need its one test bench.
pf.services.skills each needs: Gas line work needs the gas-line skill. Sewer camera needs the camera. Restores and fixture repairs at the counter need the restore skill.
pf.services.nobody home: An outdoor spigot or a crawlspace with its own access: nobody needs to be home. DONE comes with a photo.
pf.services.online: A video check only, where the owner offers it. No repair is done by video.
pf.services.extras: Travel inside the service area only (the example: 25 miles). Parts at cost or at list, the owner's pick. No tax line unless the owner sets a rate.

pf.questions.who may book: An adult. A renter books, and the landlord or manager OKs it where they pay. A person the owner of the home names may book for them.

stops the booking.words: A gas smell, hissing, or a carbon monoxide alarm
stops the booking.says: Leave the house now. Then call 911 and the gas company.
stops the booking.booking: No booking. A new request must say the gas company cleared the house.

stops the booking.words: Someone hurt, sparks, or water on wiring or a panel
stops the booking.says: Get away from the water and call 911.
stops the booking.booking: No booking until it's safe; the customer can come back.

safety steps, then the booking goes on,.words: Water spraying, flooding, or water near outlets
safety steps, then the booking goes on,.says: Shut the main water valve. Stay away from outlets and anything plugged in.

safety steps, then the booking goes on,.words: Sewage coming up into the home
safety steps, then the booking goes on,.says: Keep people and pets away, and don't run any water or drains.

safety steps, then the booking goes on,.words: No heat from a gas water heater, with no smell
safety steps, then the booking goes on,.says: Don't relight it if you smell gas. If there's no smell, the plumber checks it.

pf.visit.quotes at the visit: The plumber texts the quote with its lines before any work. The customer may OK part of it. The quote stays good 7 days.
pf.visit.extra work: Quoted by text up to the owner's limit (the example: $500). Above it, the owner OKs it first. A bigger job found gets its own quote.

pf.staff.levels: Apprentice, journeyman and master; each person's own license per state, where the state licenses plumbers.
pf.staff.supervision: An apprentice works only with a journeyman or master on the job, where the state's rules require it. An apprentice is never sent alone by default.
pf.staff.special work: Gas line work only by people with the gas-line skill, and its license where the state requires one. Lead-safe work only by people with the lead-safe card, where the rules require it.
pf.staff.who OKs what: The owner OKs fees, quotes over the limit, gas line jobs and same-day jobs. After hours, a job sent now goes to the plumber on call, then the backup set at sign-up. An office manager may OK prices if the owner sets it.
pf.staff.stand-ins: Another plumber with the same skill and level, at the same window and price.

pf.rules.license on papers: The license number on quotes and bills: from the state form.

pf.rules.state notices: A state's own notices for home repairs, like a right-to-repair notice: from the state form, sent before the work or with the quote.

pf.edges.all: Every edge case is handled the general way. These matter most for plumbing:
plumbing: The leak gets worse before the visit: the safety steps again, then urgent
A gas smell at any point: stop, get out, call 911 and the gas company
After hours: sent now to the plumber on call, then the backup; nobody takes it means no visit tonight and nothing charged
Nobody home at the door: the no-show steps, with the owner's OK before any fee
A renter whose landlord pays: the landlord's OK first, or the renter pays instead; work over the landlord's top amount goes to the landlord first
A bigger job found (a cracked drain in the wall): its own quote, OK'd by the owner over the limit
Mold, lead paint or a hazard behind a wall: stop, and a written note
A storm brings many calls: PAUSE, and a declared emergency's price limits
At the counter: a part that can't be rebuilt, a gas part, or a drop-off nobody picks up

notes:
Flow B is the plumber's usual side. The master's flow B example is already plumbing, so B is mostly the plug-in, the rename (Lee Home Services to Brightwater Plumbing, the old flowcharts' business; Jordan and Casey to Marcus and Dre) and four plumber-only changes: the after-hours price on the sent-now offer (B4-19), the water safety line when nobody on call can come (B6-18), a gas smell at the visit (B8-30), and which jobs need a permit (B10-24).
Flow A is the less usual side: the customer brings a part or a fixture to the shop counter. Sam's second company (the master's Lee's Barbershop) becomes Brightwater Supply, his plumbing parts and repair counter, with its own tax number. It loads the same plumbing plug-in, at the business.
The second kind of work in sign-up (the master's electrical) becomes heating, a common pair with plumbing: Brightwater Heating as its trade name, the electrician becomes a heating tech.
The counter's price board keeps the master's own amounts, as Brightwater Supply's example prices: faucet rebuild $35, pipe threading $40, supply lines $20, spigot rebuild $25, shower valve rebuild $55 (paid in full), pump rebuild $140 (2½ hours, the $40 fee held or a $40 deposit), faucet restore from photos ($90), fixture repair at the counter after a $25 consult. These are examples, not facts about plumbing prices.
The barbershop's color work (only Riley did it) becomes the counter's restores (only Kenny does them); the patch test becomes a part check (the old part brought in so the right one is ordered).
Sentence-sized renames: where a barbershop sentence sits in every money variant of a step (the reminder's prep line, the customer's answers, the notes), it's swapped by a phrase pair so every variant changes at once. Steps with one wording use words ops.
Flow A ops: a rush (A4-29), a landlord's five faucets (A4-32), a video check (A4-36), a leak that gets worse before the counter visit (A7-13), and a part that can't be rebuilt (A8-x01: a new part, or a plumber at home, which is flow B).
Turned off in A: the reaction-last-time first step and the child pick-up branch. A child booking reaches the master's plug-in split A4-70, which says adults only (its 'Yes, with a parent' branch is off). Nothing at a plumbing counter is booked for a child or held for a reaction.
keep: plumber, plumbing, drain, water heater and flush are the plumber's own words.
Money: B's main path is the plug-in's starting answer (the $89 service call held, Rosie texts the bill). The old example owner saved a card only, so list|card|bill and visit|card|bill are listed too. A's main path is the master's (a card saved for the $20 fee, paid at the counter).
The after-hours line (the old flowcharts' $149 call) is Brightwater's own price, said on the master's sent-now offer (B4-19). Master v1.1 now draws the rest itself: the plumber on call and the backup (S2-27, B6-16 to B6-18), no reminder and free cancel until OMW (B7-48 to B7-50), a quote OK'd in part (B8-48), the landlord's top amount and the renter paying instead (B4-37, B4-75, B8-57), a dropped call (B3-25) and the permit inspection (B10-24). The old flowcharts had the owner as the on-call backup; the master's backup is set at sign-up (S2-27: Marcus and Dre back each other up).
Money: no visit+deposit path. Brightwater holds the $89 service call for work priced at the visit; it never takes it as a deposit, so visit|deposit|bill isn't listed.
No state is named anywhere: licenses, permits, lead-safe work, deposit caps, the right to cancel and emergency prices are switches filled from each state's or city's form.
Outdated from the old flowcharts: Rosie Calendar and Book as separate tools (Rosie is the software now), and Georgia's own rules and lookups (a state's rule becomes a switch).
Master v1.2 (D24): at every plug-in split the plumber keeps its own branch and turns the others off. Both flows: the $2, no added agreement, people not spaces, no classes, work sent now. The license splits (S1-60, S1-63, S2-28) keep both branches: plumbers are licensed where the state or city licenses them, so it's state by state. Flow A (the counter): walk-ins wait in a line or a drop-off is checked in at once; a plumber's time or a pump's drop-off slot; adults only; no form, no damage hold, no crew, no date that can't move, no minimum; late means a shorter visit or the next open time; the item stays or is left; it's rated. Flow B (the home): sent now or soonest first; arrival windows; own or rent asked; a contract over the plug-in's amount; no damage hold; one plumber by name or a crew of two; no group minimum; an outside check and a permit inspection only where the job has one; a first step can be a form (the lead-safe notice).
